simple.meaning: שָׂכַר (sâkar) appears 21 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Deuteronomy, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 30:16. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, priesthood, Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׂכַר (H7936) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows שָׂכַר through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: שָׂכַר (sâkar) / H7936 is tracked through Genesis 30:16, Deuteronomy 23:5, Judges 9:4, Judges 18:4. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

Nevertheless Yahweh your God wouldn’t listen to Balaam, but Yahweh your God turned the curse into a blessing to you, because Yahweh your God loved you.
They gave him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal Berith, with which Abimelech hired vain and reckless fellows who followed him.
He said to them, “Thus and thus has Micah dealt with me, and he has hired me, and I have become his priest.”
Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread.

When the children of Ammon saw that they had become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth Rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.

For the Lord‡ The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” had made the army of the Syrians to hear the sound of chariots, and the sound of horses, even the noise of a great army; and they said to one another, “Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Egyptians to attack us.”

When the children of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon sent one thousand talents* A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds, so 1000 talents is about 30 metric tons of silver to hire chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah.

So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who came and encamped near Medeba. The children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.

The king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of Yahweh’s house. They hired masons and carpenters to restore Yahweh’s house, and also those who worked iron and bronze to repair Yahweh’s house.
He also hired one hundred thousand mighty men of valor out of Israel for one hundred talents* A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds of silver.
They hired counselors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
I discerned, and behold, God had not sent him; but he pronounced this prophecy against me. Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He hired so that I would be afraid, do so, and sin, and that they might have material for an evil report, that they might reproach me.
because they didn’t meet the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, to curse them; however our God turned the curse into a blessing.

You have sown much, and bring in little. You eat, but you don’t have enough. You drink, but you aren’t filled with drink. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm, and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes in it.”

definitions.full: H7936. sakar II. [ סָכַר ] verb hire ( = שָׂכַר ; ס erroneously for שׂ ); — only Qal Participle plural וְסֹכְרִים Ezra 4:5 and hiring against ( על ) them agents. שָׂכַר verb hire (Late Hebrew id. ; Sabean תשכר hire oneself out (?), recompense (?) DHM Hofmus. 11 ; Ethiopic hired ; Arabic reward, thank , modern Palestinian hired , of land ploughed by hire, Bergheim PEQ 1894, 196 ; Palmyrene שכרא perhaps rewarding Lzb 375 ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular ׳שׂ Deut 23:5 ; 2Kin 7:6 , suffix שְׂכָרוֺ Neh 6:12 ; 1 singular suffix שְׂכַרְתִּיךָ Gen 30:16 ; Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיִּשְׂכֹּר Judg 9:4 +, etc.; Infinitive absolute שָׂכֹר Gen 30:16 ; construct לִשְׂכֹּר 1Chr 19:6 ; Participle active שׂכֵר Prov 26:10 (twice in verse), plural שׂכְרִים 2Chr 24:12 ( Ezra 4:5 see II. סכר ); passive שָׂכוּר Neh 6:13 ; — hire , retainers Judg 9:4 ( ב pret.), soldiers, etc. 2Sam 10:6 = 1Chr 19:6-7 , 2Kin 7:6 ; 2Chr 25:6 ( ב pret.), priest Judg 18:4 , artificers Isa 46:6 ; 2Chr 24:12 , husband's favour שְׂכַרְתִּיךָ שָׂכֹר Gen 30:16 (J; ב pret.); Prov 26:10 (twice in verse) obscure, see De Now Toy; for evil purpose Deut 23:5 = Neh 13:2 ( על against ), 6:12-13 , Niph`al hire oneself out, Perfect נִשְׂכָּ֑רוּ בַּלֶּחֶם 1Sam 2:5 . Hithpa`el earn wages, Participle הַמְּשְׂתַּכֵּר Hag 1:6 (as substantive), ׳מ 1:6 (as verb, + אֶל location, construction praegn.).
definitions.rootNote: or (by permutation) סָכַר ; (Ezra 4:5), a primitive root (apparently akin (by prosthesis) to 3739 through the idea of temporary purchase; compare 7937 );
